parole.significato: what diffuses fragrance, odoriferous substances, aromatic ingredients, fragrants
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ge'ez አፈው (ʾäfäw, “scent, fragrance”), pl. አፈዋት (ʾäfäwat), if not borrowed from Old South Arabian. But also with parallels in Cushitic. The singular فُوه (fūh) is back-formed and possibly invented by medieval dictionary authors to place the word under a “root”. Doublet of فَوْعَة (fawʕ

* From the root ب ر ه ن (b r h n), interrelated or derived from the roots ب ر ه (b r h) meaning "to make white", "to clear up", "to restore to a state of youth or innocence" and ب ر ء (b r ʔ) meaning "to be free from wrong", "to be absolved from wrongdoing", "to be without blame", "to be innocent".

The whole root ج ن ز (j n z) is from Ge'ez and Old South Arabian, compare Ge'ez ገነዘ (gänäzä, “to wrap, to prepare a body for funeral”) and old Sabaean 𐩴𐩬𐩸 (gnz), 𐩴𐩬𐩸𐩩 (gnzt, “funeral”), potentially the same Iranian word as كَنْز (kanz, “treasure”).

parole.significato: place, particularly a small mountain, where victims were sacrificed in paganism, sacrificial stone
parole.testo: Borrowed from Ge'ez ገብገብ (gäbgäb) or Old South Arabian.
